title: Two Hamzahs in Two Words - when both hamzahs carry dhammah : أُ أُ
titleEn: Two Hamzahs in Two Words - when both hamzahs carry dhammah: أُ أُ
description: This situation only occurs in one place in the Quran, 46:32: أَوْلِيَآءُ أُوْلَٰىِكَ

isqat_of_the_first_hamzah.title: Isqāṭ/ḥadhf of the 1st
isqat_of_the_first_hamzah.description: Isqāṭ/ḥadhf (dropping) of the 1st of the two hamzahs.
isqat_of_the_first_hamzah.note: Imam al-Shaṭibī in line 202 mentions it is the first hamzah that is dropped. This then implies that the now present madd is a madd munfaṣil and would be read with the either qaṣr or tawassuṯ in accordance with the rules of munfaṣil for these qurra. However there are some scholars that said it is in fact the second hamzah that will be dropped, thereby making the madd a madd muttaṣil. The former opinion is the preferred opinion of most scholars.

tashil_of_first.title: Tashῑl of 1st
tashil_of_first.description: Tashῑl of 1st means to recite the first of the two hamzahs with a blend of the long vowel wāw and the second clearly (taḥqīq).
tashil_of_first.note: Both qaṣr and tawassuṯ are allowed.

tashil_of_second.title: Tashῑl of 2nd
tashil_of_second.description: Tashῑl of 2nd means to recite the first of the two hamzahs clearly (taḥqīq) and recite the second hamzah with a blend of the long vowel wāw.
tashil_of_second.note: This is one of two options for both Imams Warsh and Qunbul

ibdaal_of_second_alif_into_waw_sakinah.title: Ibdāl of 2nd to wāw sākinah
ibdaal_of_second_alif_into_waw_sakinah.description: Ibdāl of second hamzahinto a wāw sākinah - meaning the first of the two hamzahs will be read clearly (taḥqīq) and elongated as the second hamzah is now a wāw of madd.

tahqiq_of_both.title: Taḥqīq of both
tahqiq_of_both.description: Both hamzahs will be read clearly (taḥqīq) with no changes made to either.
